summary.text: Carrie Buck is the Republican nominee for Nevada's 1st Congressional District and a sitting Nevada state senator from Henderson. A longtime educator, she taught in North Las Vegas, was principal of a Henderson elementary school, and led the Pinecrest Academy charter schools before winning her Senate seat in 2020. Her campaign website says she is running on parents' rights, border security, funding police and ending taxes on tips, and the National Republican Congressional Committee has named her to its program for candidates in Democratic-held districts.

paragraphs.text: Born in Sioux City, Iowa, where she grew up; the Nevada Independent reports her father was an accountant and her mother worked for the telephone company. Her campaign website says she was raised on a small farm.
Earned a bachelor's degree in elementary education from Montana State University (1995), a master's degree from the University of Phoenix (1998), and a Ph.D. from Nova Southeastern University (2006).

Moved to Las Vegas in 1996 after college; her campaign website says she began her career teaching fifth grade in North Las Vegas. She also worked as an English-language-learner specialist and instructional coach with the Clark County School District.
Became principal of C.T. Sewell Elementary School in Henderson in 2006 and served there about eight years; she received a Milken Educator Award in 2008.

Was recruited to Pinecrest Academy of Nevada around 2014, where she was principal and executive director; became president of the Pinecrest Foundation, a nonprofit supporting charter school scholarships, in 2019.

Lost a 2016 race for Nevada State Senate District 5 to Democrat Joyce Woodhouse by fewer than 500 votes; won the open seat in 2020 after Woodhouse was termed out, and was re-elected in 2024 over Democrat Jennifer Atlas.
Committee assignments in the 2025-2026 Nevada Senate: Education; Finance; and Growth and Infrastructure.

Launched her campaign for Nevada's 1st District while serving in the state Senate; the Nevada Independent reports she has President Donald Trump's endorsement. She won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary.

Her campaign website says she and her husband Eric, a retired Deputy Chief of Police, have four sons and are local small business owners; in a 2024 Ballotpedia survey she described herself as the wife of a Henderson police captain and mother of four sons, two of whom serve in the U.S. Armed Forces.
